Astro's current biases on bitcoin:native - update

Update on my current biases, always going top-down in timeframes.

Mentioning explicitly here because I operate on many timeframes and biases can be confused if timeframe isn't clear.

➡️Macro (Monthly/Weekly): as you know, still very bullish, I think 60k is the bottom and the bears are wrong and $btc is never going to 50k.
➡️Positional (Daily timeframes): No longer bullish because I think the move is done for the most part, we don't move higher until September closes at least. That's a full month of nothing so no reason to be bullish here. Positional long TP'ing process is ongoing.
➡️Swing (Hourly timeframes): Bearish and I expect a local pullback paired with red September and I am short for it.
➡️Scalp (minute timeframes): not interested at the moment. Recent idea of weekly fake open pump mentioned.

Always open the corresponding timeframe on a chart before applying/considering my bias.

tweets.text:
$btc - my higher timeframe call range idea

An hourly range ✅, a daily range ✅, and... a weekly range also very close now to completion ⏳

With all the fomo on the timeline and how everyone "called the bottom", I think there may be some frustration to the ones who did not bet (big) on catching (part of) this quite substantial move.

Our range idea also gently explains why the move from 69k -> 78k by now, a whopping 9k move in just a few days, went so fast. And also why I went confidently long on it with large size, but also how a decent amount has already been completed.

So I think a more grounded post next now is key. To just to remind you of our call we made month and a half ago, of how in the end, this is just the completion of our series of ranges we presented.

It doesn't mean we can't go higher, and it doesn't mean we won't go to new ath's, you all know our base bottom thesis we have constructed begin February.

But it does mean that with the weekly range completing, we can at least expect the state of price delivery to slow significantly.

And I want to be clear:

In hindsight, it will look easy what has happened near weekly range high. But we are trying to predict and trade, and that's quite different than hindsight.

It's not as simple as: "weekly range high will reverse and send us back down, go ahead and use a 100x short at exactly the weekly range".

There could simply be a consolidation.

We need deeper analysis which I will be posting in the time to come. We also look at $eth as it is slightly ahead in the race towards its weekly range high.

I also hinted about the monthly range, which I will expand upon later.

And, despite the range idea completing on $btc, there is always a delay on other crypto assets who aren't as far on their range idea which is where opportunity sits.

So as of now, it's good to recognize that our range idea is slowly completing, where it's at, and what I am looking for over the next weeks.

It also confirms why I longed 69k so confidently despite already seeing green candles at that time, since it's that weekly midrange point and daily range breakout point, where all resistance disappears until weekly range high approaches.

I thank you, and I will see you in the near future.

tweets.text:
So hinted this before but putting it out there now, since that is what I believe my followers need the most right now.

Extensive post is below. But here's a short version/quick recap if you missed the bottom/breakout and genuinely feel frozen out:

🥇 First priority: don't lose money.
Don't revenge short, don't short "back to your entry", and don't stay stubbornly bearish just because you missed the move.

🥈 Accept the conditions changed.
We're trending up. That doesn't mean straight up, it means HH → HL → HH → HL. Flip the switch from trying to fade everything to understanding you're in a buyers market.

🥉 Then focus on buying dips, not chasing local tops.
You don't need insanely complex TA for this. Support/resistance, the right EMA, liquidation flushes, simple TA works when you correctly understand the market conditions.

Effective TA can be very easy, but understanding the conditions of the market is hard m yet only the latter makes the former work.

Buy dips with conviction, let price move away, then manage profit accordingly.

If leveraged, take significant exposure off before the next expected flush. If spot, focus more on slowly selling into the eventual overall market top.

You haven't missed the opportunity to make money.

You're simply dealing with different conditions now imo.

Money-making potential in a market never ends.

An imo timely reminder.
